title: PL/I's ON-Units: Structured Exception Handling Before It Had the Name
explainer: Decades before Python's `try`/`except` or JavaScript's `try`/`catch`, IBM's PL/I — designed in the mid-1960s — introduced ON-units: blocks of code registered in advance to run automatically when a named condition such as ZERODIVIDE or SUBSCRIPTRANGE occurred during a program's execution. That handler-registered-ahead-of-time model, inherited down through called procedures much like a Python exception propagates up a call stack, was one of the earliest structured alternatives to just checking a return code after every operation.
